name: Moon buggy
what_i_did: A single-rider charcoal quad: four balloon tyres with staggered tread blocks, curved fenders hugging each tyre, exposed A-arms and coil-over shocks, a split twin-pod nose with headlights, a fuel tank rising to the handlebars and a light pod, a saddle seat and a long kicked-up tail with a red tail light. Wheels are named nodes (Wheel_FL/FR/RL/RR) and turn as it drives.
good: Silhouette of the sheet: big tyres, short wheelbase, split nose, tall bars, long tail.
Charcoal #3a4a5a and panel grey #4a5a6a straight from the spec sheet.
Leaves lasting twin tyre tracks in the dust as it drives (MB1).
off: Headlights are pale ice-white, not the sheet's cyan: on the Moon cyan is reserved for the meteorite and the Star Child (study rule). Easy to flip if Evan wants the sheet's cyan.
No cyan accent strips along the seams, for the same reason.
Engine and frame detail between the wheels is simpler than the sheet's mechanical clutter.
About 22k triangles, most in the tread blocks; can be halved if the tile needs it.

rounds.t: First build: flat paddle fenders, thin tyres.
Fatter balloon tyres (0.42 m wide), 14 chunky tread rows, fenders bent round each tyre, bigger raised nose pods, tail kicked up 12 degrees.
